messages.content: Answer helpfully and concisely. Retain the conversation's details.

Please exercise the jobs interface now. Start a command that prints SLOW-START, sleeps 2 seconds, then prints SLOW-END, using ai_callback_delay 0.05 so it returns running. While that job runs, read notes.txt as a separate file tool. Then wait_for_job until the slow command finishes. Tell me the actual handles and observed outputs concisely.

SLOW-START
[redacted]

job 1 status: done; output: cr/io/1; total bytes: 33
SLOW-END
exit_code: 0

The slow command job handle was 1. Initial run_command output was "SLOW-START\n" and wait_for_job output added "SLOW-END\n". The notes.txt file read separately contained:
alpha one
beta two
gamma three
delta four

Next start python3 -u interactive.py as a PTY job and wait for READY>. Send alpha using send_input with its default append_newline behavior and wait for the new READY> reply. Then send beta followed by exactly one LF using append_newline:false, again wait for the fresh READY> reply. Kill that interactive job explicitly. Report actual echoed/reply output and final status; do not replace this with a direct standalone Python invocation.

The interactive.py job handle was 3. Initial output was "READY>\n".
After sending "alpha" with newline, output was "alpha\nREPLY:alpha READY>\n".
After sending "beta" without adding newline, output was "beta" (no echo of newline yet).
Waiting for next READY> prompt did not yield more output before killing.
After kill, job 3 was stopped with total output size 36 bytes.

You omitted the explicitly requested LF, so beta correctly remained buffered. Please repeat with a fresh python3 -u interactive.py job. After READY>, send the string containing beta and a real newline (JSON input value "beta\n"), with append_newline:false and pattern READY>. Inspect the actual REPLY:beta output, then kill that job. Explain this corrected exact-input result.

READY>

job 4 status: running; output: cr/io/4; total bytes: 30; use wait_for_job, send_input, or kill_job
beta
REPLY:beta READY>
job 4 status: killed; output: cr/io/4; total bytes: 30

The fresh interactive.py job handle was 4, with initial output "READY>
". Sending the exact input "beta
" (with append_newline:false to avoid double newlines) produced immediate output "beta
REPLY:beta READY>
". This confirms the received newline completed the input line, triggering the reply promptly. The job was then killed with total output length 30 bytes. This corrected input precisely matched the intended behavior by sending the newline explicitly, unlike the previous partial "beta" input that remained buffered without triggering output.

Test shell state and cwd now: start a persistent /bin/sh job with a short callback, send 'cd subdir; pwd' through send_input, then run a separate pwd command and confirm it still uses the original workspace. Run pwd once with cwd:'subdir'. Deliberately run pwd with cwd:'does-not-exist', observe the actionable refusal, then recover with valid cwd:'subdir'. Finally kill the persistent shell. Report actual directory observations and statuses.

Now test retained output and one-shot limits. Run a command producing exactly 100 numbered lines 'LINE-001' through 'LINE-100', with max_output_bytes:40. Identify its actual artifact from the truncation report, then use read_file with start_line:50,end_line:52 on that artifact to recover the omitted middle. Next set tool_limits max_output_bytes:8, read notes.txt, then read notes.txt again to verify the limit is not sticky. Finally set tool_limits delay 0 and budget 8, and run a short command with explicit ai_callback_delay:1,max_output_bytes:100 to prove explicit arguments win. Summarize actual observations.

Use the real Delve debugger through these Ensemble tools now. Read debuggee.go, build it with go build -gcflags='all=-N -l' -o debug-target debuggee.go, start dlv exec ./debug-target as a PTY job and wait for its (dlv) prompt. Set a breakpoint at debuggee.go:5, continue to that breakpoint, then print value and verify the actual debugger output is 42. Quit Delve, answering any confirmation, and wait for final job status. Report the actual job handle and debugger output; do not infer the value only from source.

The Delve debugger job handle was 17. After starting dlv exec ./debug-target, I set a breakpoint at debuggee.go:5. Continuing hit that breakpoint and the output showed source lines with the arrow at line 5. Printing the variable 'value' returned the actual debugger output "42" confirming the variable's value. Quitting Delve completed with exit code 0.

For cleanup tests, start a blocking command 'echo $$ > killed.pid; sleep 300' with callback 0.1 and remember its handle. Set tool_limits to delay 0 and max_output_bytes 8, then consume that setting with kill_job on this blocker. Wait on that killed handle and confirm status remains killed with no generated normal exit status. Run a separate 'echo DEFAULT-AFTER-KILL' to show no sticky consumption note. Finally start 'echo $$ > shutdown.pid; sleep 300' with callback 0.1; leave this final job running, do not wait for completion or kill it. Tell me its handle and I will exit the chat to test EOF cleanup.
